facts.title: Ankylosaurs Had Tail Clubs Strong Enough to Break Bone
facts.summary: Ankylosaurus and its relatives, the ankylosaurids, carried a bony club at the end of the tail, and a 2009 study found that adult clubs were capable of breaking bone.

facts.title: Argentinosaurus Was One of the Heaviest Animals Ever to Walk the Earth
facts.summary: Argentinosaurus, a giant titanosaur from Argentina, is among the largest land animals known, with published weight estimates ranging from about 60 to 96 tonnes.

facts.title: Birds Are Living Dinosaurs Descended From Theropods
facts.summary: Birds are not just related to dinosaurs; they are dinosaurs, the only lineage that survived.

facts.title: Dinosaurs Lived on Every Continent, Including Antarctica
facts.summary: Dinosaur fossils have been found on all seven continents, including Antarctica.

facts.title: Maiasaura Was a Caring Parent That Raised Its Young in Nesting Colonies
facts.summary: Maiasaura, a duck-billed dinosaur from Montana, gave scientists some of the first strong evidence that dinosaurs cared for their young.

facts.title: Microraptor Was a Four-Winged Dinosaur That Could Glide
facts.summary: Microraptor, a small dromaeosaurid dinosaur from China, had long flight feathers on its arms, legs and tail, giving it four wings.

facts.title: Pachycephalosaurus Had a 25 cm Thick Skull Dome That May Have Been Used in Fights
facts.summary: Pachycephalosaurus had a solid bony dome on its skull up to about 25 cm (10 in) thick, and injuries on fossil domes suggest it may have used it in fights.

facts.title: Pterosaurs Were Not Dinosaurs, but Their Flying Reptile Cousins
facts.summary: Pterosaurs, the winged reptiles that often appear beside dinosaurs in films and books, were not dinosaurs.

facts.title: Dinosaurs Were Neither Fully Warm-Blooded Nor Cold-Blooded
facts.summary: A 2014 study in Science concluded that dinosaurs were neither cold-blooded like modern reptiles nor fully warm-blooded like mammals, but somewhere in between.

facts.title: Titanosaurs Nearly 45 Feet Long Hatched as Babies of Just 15 Inches
facts.summary: At Auca Mahuevo in Patagonia, Argentina, titanosaur sauropods that grew to nearly 45 feet (about 14 m) long laid eggs whose embryos would have hatched at a mere 15 inches (about 38 cm).

facts.title: Spinosaurus Was Longer Than T. rex and Built for Hunting in Water
facts.summary: Spinosaurus, a predatory dinosaur that lived in North Africa 95 to 100 million years ago, was probably longer than Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.title: The Asteroid That Killed the Dinosaurs Was 10 km Wide and Hit at 72,000 km/h
facts.summary: About 66 million years ago, an asteroid roughly 10 kilometres wide slammed into what is now the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico.

facts.title: The K-Pg Mass Extinction Wiped Out About 75% of Species, Not Just Dinosaurs
facts.summary: The mass extinction that ended the age of dinosaurs about 66 million years ago killed roughly three-quarters of all plant and animal species on Earth.

facts.title: The Longest Dinosaur Name Has 23 Letters: Micropachycephalosaurus
facts.summary: Micropachycephalosaurus, a small plant-eater from Late Cretaceous China, has the longest name of any dinosaur: 23 letters.

facts.title: The Word 'Dinosaur' Was Coined in 1842 and Means 'Terrible Lizard'
facts.summary: The word 'dinosaur' was coined by the British anatomist and palaeontologist Richard Owen and first appeared in print in April 1842.

facts.title: Triceratops Had Up to 800 Teeth and Replaced Them Throughout Its Life
facts.summary: Triceratops had between 432 and 800 teeth, packed into stacked batteries and replaced continuously throughout its life.

facts.title: Velociraptor Was Actually Turkey-Sized and Covered in Feathers
facts.summary: The real Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey.
